study type: Experimental animal study (mice) complemented by a human cross-sectional study
exposure: Maternal Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) infection during pregnancy (mice)
outcome: Resistance to CHIKV challenge in offspring (mice)
Viral loads in offspring's brain and spleen (mice)
CHIKV RNA and proteins in maternal breast tissue and milk (mice)
Presence of CHIKV RNA in colostrum samples (humans)
cohort: The study included pregnant BALB/c female mice and their offspring, as well as healthy lactating women.
finding: Breastfeeding by Chikungunya virus-infected dams confers immune protection against subsequent CHIKV challenge in adult mouse offspring, correlating with the presence of viral RNA in human colostrum.
cross-section timing: Colostrum samples from healthy lactating women (implying shortly after birth)
